output.brief: The departures are concentrated on one matter. Eight of the 11 associates on Kestrel have resigned, against 1 of the 13 who never worked on it. Every Kestrel associate reports to Dorian Faulk, and he supervises no one else. That pattern argues against a pay explanation, the firm-wide hours target and ordinary market movement. Those would hit all associates in the group and other groups too, and the other groups are at their normal rates. The survey comments point to both heavy workload and harsh supervision, but the records cannot tell the two apart, because everyone on Kestrel has the same partner. I am fairly confident the cause is something specific to Kestrel. I am not sure whether the workload, the supervision or both are responsible. Do not announce the £12k group-wide retention payment and close the review. It would miss the cause and cost £228k. Run the confidential outside interviews (about £9k, three weeks). Four leavers have already agreed to take part. Structure them to separate supervision from workload. Meanwhile consider an interim step that is cheap to reverse, and add matter and supervising-partner fields to attrition reporting. Decide on supervision changes or contract reviewers once the interviews are in. The document-review phase runs to the end of December.
